top_signal.title: I compared what LLC formation companies charge vs. what things actually cost. The markups are wild.
top_signal.summary: I've been digging into the LLC formation industry for a project I'm building, and I wanted to share the numbers because I wish someone had told me this before I almost paid for all of it:    EIN filing: $50–$99 charged vs. $0 actual.  The IRS gives you an EIN free in about 10 minutes on their website. There is no filing, no paperwork, no waiting period. Companies charge up to $99 to fill out a web form for you.    Compliance/deadline tracking: $99–$299/yr charged vs. $0 actual.  This is just calendar reminders for your annual report. The deadlines are public record on every Secretary of State site. You're paying $200/yr for someone to email you a date.    Registered agent service: $125–$299/yr charged vs. $0 actual (for many people).  If you have a physical address in your state and someone's there during business hours, you can legally be your own registered agent in most states. Half the people paying for this don't need to.    Operating agreement templates: $35–$149 charged vs. free templates everywhere.  It's a standard document. The paid versions aren't meaningfully better than what's freely available.   I'm not saying these companies are scams — formation filing itself is a real service. But the upsells are priced on the assumption that you won't look up the alternative. So look up the alternative.
